This Agreement shall terminate immediately upon notice if either party becomes insolvent (i.e., becomes unable to pay its debts in the ordinary course of business as they come due) or makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors. reasons: Rule correctly applied: Section 11.3 covers only survival and a generic return-or-destroy of Confidential Information, with no transition assistance, data export or certified deletion mechanic, so an insert is the right operation for this hosting/ASP agreement.

Directionality is correct — the obligation runs from Commerce One (vendor/licensor) to Corio (our client, the customer/ASP), and covers Corio's Customers' and Software Users' data flowing through MarketSite.net.

Inserted Section 11.4 tracks the preferred position and model language: up to six (6) months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return of data in a commonly used machine-readable format within thirty (30) days, and certified deletion thereafter; the 'Notwithstanding Section 11.3' lead-in sensibly prevents the existing return-or-destroy sentence from defeating the new right.
Minimal-edit discipline observed: p0098 is left verbatim and the new obligation is added as a separate paragraph in the termination section.
Comment is accurate, concise, in-voice, cites the playbook position and offers the 90-day fallback while holding the data return and deletion certificate.

input.quote: MarketSite.net Access Fee: Due upon Software Acceptance, and on each annual anniversary of Software Acceptance thereafter.
input.rationale: Exhibit B commits Corio (our party) to a flat annual MarketSite.net Access Fee (Year 1 and Years 2-5 and beyond, p0153) payable on each anniversary across a five-year initial term (p0096) that can only be exited for material breach or insolvency (p0097) — a de facto multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right, which is our walk-away position. In addition, the revenue share in p0158 is measured against a deemed "minimum limitation of 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer" rather than actual usage, creating a minimum charge untethered from consumption. Our preferred position is fees for usage or ordered services only; the minimal fallback edit adds a 30 days' notice discontinuation right with a pro-rata true-up instead of any penalty or shortfall charge, and ties the revenue share to actual Authorized Software Users. Commitments Commerce One makes to us (e.g., its MarketSite transaction revenue share in p0156) are unaffected.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Parties: we represent Corio Inc.; counterparty is Commerce One, Inc..

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

**Finding submitted: deviation (MINCOMMIT), confidence 0.62.**

What I found:
- **No express "minimum purchase" or "take or pay" clause** exists, but the economics operate as one: Exhibit B fixes a flat annual **MarketSite.net Access Fee** (Year 1; Years 2–5 and beyond, p0153) payable "on each annual anniversary" (p0168) across a **five-year initial term** (p0096) exitable only for material breach or insolvency (p0097) — a multi-year commitment with no reduction or termination right, i.e. our walk-away position.
- Secondary hit: the Application Management revenue share is measured against a **deemed "minimum limitation of 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer"** (p0158) rather than actual usage.
- Direction checked: maintenance fees are already conditional on Corio electing to continue (4.2), Exhibit D cooperation is expressly **non-binding** (p0198), and Commerce One's revenue-share commitment to us (p0156) was left untouched.

Redline (validated, ok:true) — fallback level, minimal edits:
1. p0168 — adds a right for Corio to discontinue MarketSite.net access on **30 days' notice**, stopping further annual fees, with a **pro-rata true-up "without penalty, shortfall or termination charge."**
2. p0158 — replaces the deemed 40-user minimum with the **actual number** of Authorized Software Users.

You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Exhibit B commits Corio (our party) to a flat annual MarketSite.net Access Fee (Year 1 and Years 2-5 and beyond, p0153) payable on each anniversary across a five-year initial term (p0096) that can only be exited for material breach or insolvency (p0097) — a de facto multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right, which is our walk-away position. In addition, the revenue share in p0158 is measured against a deemed "minimum limitation of 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer" rather than actual usage, creating a minimum charge untethered from consumption. Our preferred position is fees for usage or ordered services only; the minimal fallback edit adds a 30 days' notice discontinuation right with a pro-rata true-up instead of any penalty or shortfall charge, and ties the revenue share to actual Authorized Software Users. Commitments Commerce One makes to us (e.g., its MarketSite transaction revenue share in p0156) are unaffected.

Original paragraphs:
p0168: MarketSite.net Access Fee: Due upon Software Acceptance, and on each annual anniversary of Software Acceptance thereafter.
p0158: A. No Application Management Revenue shall be due for any Corio Customer subscriptions utilizing the initial 3000 Software User licenses granted herein, subject to a minimum limitation of 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer
p0096: 11.1 Term. The term of this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue in full force and effect for an initial period of five (5) years. Thereafter, this Agreement shall automatically renew for subsequent one (1) year periods unless either party provides the other party with written notification at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the initial five (5) year term or any one (1) year renewal thereof of its intention to terminate this Agreement.
p0153: MARKETSITE.NET SERVICE FEES: MarketSite.net Service Access: Year 1 [*] Year 2-5, and beyond: [*]

Resolved definitions:
SOFTWARE USER: 1.1 "SOFTWARE USER" means a named user of the Corio Services worldwide to whom a user identification number and password has been assigned, which permits that user to access and use the Software on a designated Corio Server. The identification number and password used by a Software User is reusable and reassignable and may be used and transferred by Corio, in accordance with the licenses granted below, between Customers as one Customer discontinues the Corio Services and another Customer subscribes.
APPLICATION MANAGEMENT REVENUE: 1.2.5 "APPLICATION MANAGEMENT REVENUE" means net revenue Corio receives from Customers for Tier One support of the Software and MarketSite Service, operational support of the Software and MarketSite Service and basic infrastructure support (hardware, database and operating system) for the Software and MarketSite Service. Net revenue means all revenue received by Corio from Customers for the Software and MarketSite Service, less taxes, freight, insurance, refunds or credits and other non-product items.
SOFTWARE: 1.10 "SOFTWARE" means Commerce One's proprietary software described in EXHIBIT A attached hereto and made a part hereof, in object code form only, and any Updates or Upgrades (as defined below) thereto.

p0168: MarketSite.net Access Fee: Due upon Software Acceptance, and on each annual anniversary of Software Acceptance thereafter; provided that Corio may discontinue its access to the MarketSite.net Service upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One, in which case no further annual MarketSite.net Access Fee shall accrue and the parties shall true-up amounts due for access actually provided through the effective date of discontinuation, without penalty, shortfall or termination charge.
p0158: A. No Application Management Revenue shall be due for any Corio Customer subscriptions utilizing the initial 3000 Software User licenses granted herein, calculated on the actual number of Authorized Software Users per Customer

We have added a 30 days' notice discontinuation right with a pro-rata true-up (no penalty or shortfall charge) and tied the revenue share to actual Authorized Software Users.

Searches for \"liquidated damages\", \"penalt\", \"interest\" and \"minimum\" return no customer-payable stipulated-damages provisions. Section 11 termination contains no termination fee or accelerated/minimum payment; the only post-termination payments (11.3) are for continued use of the Software by existing customers, i.e. value actually received. GRANT OF RIGHTS.","rationale":"Direction: Commerce One (Vendor/Licensor) grants; Corio (our party) is the licensee, so the grant scope is ours to widen. Commerce One likewise has no convenience right, which matches the preferred position, so the minimal fix is to insert a new Section 11.4 giving Corio a 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees and no early-termination penalty, while confirming that Commerce One may not walk away mid-term.","proposal":"Add Corio right to terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund and no penalty; confirm Commerce One has no convenience right during the term","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-d4a99bc4","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 14 MISCELLANEOUS.","rationale":"Section 14.1 is mutual and does contain an M&A/asset-sale carve-out, so it is above walk-away, but it falls short of our preferred position in two respects: (i) there is no carve-out for assignment to our affiliates (so internal reorganizations require Commerce One's consent), and (ii) the direct-competitor exception applies symmetrically, giving Commerce One a consent veto over our own merger, acquisition or asset sale whenever the acquirer competes with Commerce One — effectively a change-of-control consent right against us. Consent is also not subject to any reasonableness standard. Section 11 contains no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right, so no deletion is needed there. The redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out for Corio, confines the competitor-consent exception to Commerce One's assignments (protecting us from a Commerce One assignment to a Corio competitor), and makes any remaining consent subject to a reasonableness standard.","proposal":"Add affiliate/successor assignment right for Corio without consent, limit competitor-consent exception to Commerce One assignments, and add a reasonableness standard for consent.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-bb933cea","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 4 FEES.","rationale":"Section 4.4 binds us (Corio) to an audit of books and records verifying amounts payable to Commerce One. It already meets several playbook requirements: once per calendar year, independent CPA reasonably acceptable to us, Commerce One bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%. It deviates in that notice is only \"reasonable notice\" rather than a fixed 30 days' written notice, timing is only \"reasonable times\" rather than business hours, and the auditor is not expressly bound by confidentiality; there is also no express bar on access to our systems. The redline supplies these limits with a single minimal replacement, leaving frequency and cost allocation untouched.","proposal":"Add 30 days' written notice, business-hours limit, auditor confidentiality undertaking and no-systems-access to the Section 4.4 audit right","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-3be8a825","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 14 MISCELLANEOUS.","rationale":"Section 14.3 selects California law, which is on the accepted list (fallback), but imposes mandatory single-arbitrator AAA arbitration in San Francisco rather than court adjudication. The playbook requires courts as the dispute forum. Because the arbitration seat is domestic (not abroad), this is a medium deviation rather than walk-away. Given both parties are California-based and California law is an accepted jurisdiction, we take the fallback position: keep California law and substitute exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in San Francisco County, deleting only the arbitration mechanics and the AAA fee allocation that becomes inoperative.","proposal":"Replace mandatory AAA arbitration with exclusive jurisdiction of California state and federal courts in San Francisco County; retain California governing law.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-indemn-8035eb87","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 8 INDEMNIFICATION.","rationale":"Section 8.1 does provide a vendor-side third-party IP infringement indemnity for the Software in favour of Corio and its Customers, with standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics and procure-modify-refund remedies, and Section 9 carves Section 8 out of the liability cap, so the core IP limb of the rule is satisfied and there is no offsetting Corio indemnity. The playbook's preferred position is \"No non-solicit on Customer,\" which the document already achieves, so no redline and no counterparty comment are warranted and all paragraphs are left unchanged. The residual deterministic checks for a 12-month duration and a general-solicitation carve-out cannot be satisfied here because there is no covenant to narrow; satisfying them would require inserting a restriction on our own client, which is contrary to the preferred position and to our client's interest. § 14.10 is cited solely as the scope anchor: it incorporates a separate Non-Disclosure Agreement and Statement of Work, and if either of those documents contains a non-solicit we would hold it to the fallback (mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and no no-hire).","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-renewal-445f12d0","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 11 TERM AND TERMINATION.","rationale":"Section 11.1 already meets the core preferred position: renewals are 12 months and either party (including us as licensee) can exit on 30 days' written notice, so no walk-away trigger (no multi-year renewals, notice window well under 90 days). Two preferred elements are missing: (i) no Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal, and (ii) no cap on renewal-term price increases — Exhibit B only states \"Year 2-5, and beyond: [*]\" for maintenance/support and MarketSite fees, leaving renewal uplift unconstrained. As the customer/ASP whose Customers' data flows through Commerce One's MarketSite.net Service, we need a defined exit path. Inserted a new Section 11.4 matching the preferred position: up to six (6) months of transition assistance at Commerce One's then-current rates, return of our and our Customers' data in a commonly used machine-readable format within thirty (30) days, and certified deletion thereafter, expressly overriding the generic return-or-destroy sentence in Section 11.3.","proposal":"Insert new Section 11.4 requiring Commerce One to provide up to six months of transition assistance and to return, then certify deletion of, Corio and Customer data.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-warranty-3af50c88","ruleId":"WARRANTY","ruleTitle":"Performance warranty and duration","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 8 7 WARRANTIES AND DISCLAIMER.","rationale":"Section 7.3 gives a conformance-to-Documentation warranty but only for sixty (60) days measured from the Effective Date and capped at December 31, 1999. That is below both the preferred 12-month software period and the 90-day fallback, and because Acceptance Testing under Section 3.1 can run through December 31, 1999, the Warranty Period could lapse before or at acceptance, leaving us with effectively no conformance warranty. Under the playbook we require CGL of USD 1M/2M, E&O of USD 2M, cyber of USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation and certificates on request. Inserted as new Section 14.10 in Miscellaneous, with the existing entire-agreement clause renumbered 14.11.","proposal":"Insert an insurance covenant as new Section 14.10 requiring Commerce One to carry CGL, E&O, cyber and workers' compensation coverage and to furnish certificates.","verification":"pass"}]

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.5 (Corio / Commerce One Agreement)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side — Corio) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the hosting/licence agreement; verified findings only

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the agreement against our playbook and identified **18 findings**: 2 critical deviations, 2 high-severity items requiring change (1 deviation, 1 missing), 8 medium items (6 deviations, 2 missing), 1 low missing item, 5 compliant positions, and 1 finding that failed verification and is not relied upon below.

The two critical issues are commercial gating items. First, **§ 13.5 (Developments)** flips ownership of interface coding and programs created solely by Corio to Commerce One whenever Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis, with no licence back — an assignment of our IP to the vendor, and the agreement is silent on non-assignment of Corio and Customer data hosted on the Corio Servers. Second, the **§ 9 liability cap** is nominally mutual but is limited to amounts "actually paid" for "the transaction which the liability relates to", with no US$1,000,000 floor and carve-outs only for § 8; there are no carve-outs for confidentiality/security (§ 10), gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement.

Beyond these, the commercial structure is one-sided on exit and volume: a **five-year initial term terminable only for uncured material breach or insolvency (§ 11.1–11.2)** with no convenience right for us, no post-termination transition assistance or data return mechanic, and an **Exhibit B flat annual MarketSite.net Access Fee** payable across the five years plus a revenue share computed on a deemed minimum of 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer rather than actual usage. The **§ 7.3 warranty period** (60 days from the Effective Date, capped at 31 December 1999) may lapse before Acceptance Testing under § 3.1 concludes, and there is no professional-services warranty. Smaller items: no affiliate/contractor extension of the § 2 licences (despite § 14.8 contemplating subcontracting), § 14.1 assignment gaps, § 4.4 audit mechanics, mandatory AAA arbitration in § 14.3, indemnity scope in § 8, renewal-pricing protection in § 11.1, and no insurance covenant.

Helpfully, several playbook positions are already met with no redline required: no exclusivity obligation on us, no liquidated damages or penalties payable by us, no non-compete or field-of-use covenant binding us, and no MFN burdening us.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue / position |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 13 Shared Resources (§ 13.5) | Ownership of Developments flips to Commerce One where it provides ongoing support, with no licence back; no confirmation that Corio/Customer data is not assigned. Redline: we retain ownership, Commerce One takes a nonexclusive royalty-free support licence, plus data non-assignment confirmation. |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 9 Limitation of Liability | Cap limited to amounts "actually paid" for the related transaction; no US$1m floor; carve-outs only for § 8. Redline: greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and US$1,000,000, mutual, plus Excluded Claims for indemnities, confidentiality/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement. Fallback: straight 12 months' fees with those carve-outs. |
| 3 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § 11 Term and Termination | Five-year initial term with one-year auto-renewals; termination only for uncured material breach or insolvency. Redline: new § 11.4 giving us 30-day convenience right with pro-rata refund and no penalty; confirm Commerce One has no convenience right mid-term. |
| 4 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 3 (Grant of Rights, § 2) | "Affiliate" appears nowhere and no grant names contractors, though § 14.8 contemplates subcontracting and servers may be "operated by or for Corio". Redline: new § 2.11 extending § 2 licences to our affiliates and contractors, with us responsible for compliance. Fallback: affiliate coverage on written notice. |
| 5 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments | Deviation | § 17 Payment Terms / Exhibit B | Flat annual MarketSite.net Access Fee across a five-year term with no reduction or exit right (de facto take-or-pay), and revenue share measured on a deemed 40-user minimum. Redline: 30 days' notice reduction/discontinuation right with pro-rata true-up; revenue share tied to actual Authorized Software Users. |
| 6 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Deviation | § 8 / § 7 Warranties and Disclaimer (§ 7.3) | 60-day warranty from the Effective Date, capped at 31 December 1999, may expire before or at acceptance under § 3.1; no professional-services warranty. Redline: 12 months from acceptance plus services warranty with re-performance/refund. Fallback: 90 days. |
| 7 | Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | Missing | § 11 Term and Termination | No transition, migration, data export or data-return mechanic; § 12 covers only source code escrow on Release Conditions. Redline: new § 11.4 — up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, data return in a machine-readable format within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter. |
